messages:
Dana: Quick follow-up from the onboarding lane: proposing we split the runtime-handshake checks into two separate phases: deterministic ABI/manifest validation at intake, and behavioral smokeflows run asynchronously. This keeps the hot path tight.
Leo: sounds sensible. can you outline what counts as deterministic vs behavioral?
Dana: deterministic = manifest schema, tokenizer fingerprint, kv-manifest presence, shape metadata, and exported ops list. behavioral = golden-delta checks, kv-exercise, perf microbench under target seqlens.
Priya: how does the gateway get an answer fast enough to allow immediate pinning? we can't block API creation on full smoke.
Dana: gateway would call intake-validator sync and get a simple verdict: PASS/DEFER/REJECT plus an idempotency token. PASS allows provisional pin; DEFER returns decisionId. DEFER flows into async smokeflow queue.
Omar: what happens if provisional pin later fails smokeflow? immediate rollback? can we avoid user-facing flaps?
Dana: plan: provisional pin is labeled "soft-active"; runtime treats soft-active as candidate and prefers it only if safe. If smokeflow fails, coordinator emits a quarantine event; runtime switches traffic back to last pinned stable model with a 60s canary-weighted drain to avoid cache storms.
Yuki: we need strong audit trail. each decision should have a compact provenance record and pointer to full artifacts.
Dana: yes coordinator writes an append-only record to ledger (decision_id, manifest_hash, verdict_summary, proof_uri). full artifacts go to object store. ledger events are what runtime subscribes to.
build-bot: CI: regulator-tests triggered for onboarding-smokeflow (#1290).
Leo: thresholds: for quantized builds we saw variability. prefer MAD-based thresholds instead of simple mean diff.
Priya: agree. coordinator will compute MAD per-golden-bucket and allow per-quant-profile multipliers. ops can tune per-tenant.
Omar: job deduping? many teams resubmit same artifact during a CI loop. we need idempotency on manifest+artifact version+submitter.
Dana: idempotency key = sha256(manifest) + artifact_version + submitter_email. coordinator returns existing decision_id if key seen.
Yuki: telemetry: need tags for quick filtering (e.g., "fastpass_reasons=lint,token_ok"). keep payload compact for runtime lookups.
Dana: verdict payload will be small: {decision_id, status, tags[], proof_uri}. Full JSON in object store. ledger stores flattened fields for query.
Leo: what about SLOs? product wants fullbench under 20m for common models. heavy models will be best-effort. coordinator should return ETA in decision.
Priya: propose 3 tiers: quick (<2B) 8-12m, medium (2-8B) 12-30m, large >8B best-effort. we'll expose ETA and a cost_estimate in gpu_minutes.
Omar: runtime handshake: KV manifest schema has changed a bit. we must ensure runtime library validates at startup and can decline loading incompatible models.
Dana: intake-validator will assert required kv fields and a runtime-compat flag. runtime will still perform a last-mile KV smoke on load; if it fails, it reports back to coordinator and we quarantine.
Yuki: test plan? need deterministic tests for validator and fuzz tests for smokeflows. Also a stress test for many concurrent deferred jobs.
Dana: eng-ml will add unit tests for validator, a fuzz harness for golden noise, and a load test for coordinator queuing. I'll open three PRs.
Leo: ok. I'll draft a short RFC with API shapes: POST /intake/validate -> verdict|decision_id, GET /decisions/{id}, webhook subscription for ledger events.
Priya: +1. I'll own telemetry tag schema and MAD multipliers doc.
Omar: i'll update runtime loader doc to react to ledger quarantine events and add canary drain recipe.
Dana: thanks all. plan to sync Friday 10am to review RFC and test matrix. ping me if you want to pair earlier. :thumbsup:
